events.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
events.description: Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations. After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas. Continue reading...

events.title: Thursday briefing: What we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang and the Nvidia affair
events.description: In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies. Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines. UK | Ministers are considering changing the law to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand. Climate | The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country. US midterms | Democrat Scott Colom has become the first Black senator in Mississippi to be elected since Reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states. Europe | Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years , setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power. Technology | Police officers risk arresting innocent people , especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found. Continue reading...
events.ticker_label: 🪖 Thursday briefing: What we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang and the Nvidia affair

events.description: EU leaders in Dublin were called on by an AI executive to move quickly in the tech race with the US and China. EU official Metsola, however, expressed frustration with the idea that the bloc is behind in AI development.

events.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
events.description: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

events.title: Why does El Salvador's Bukele have troops in Haiti?
events.description: Haiti's Prime Minister congratulating El Salvador's President for a gang crackdown in Haiti has shone a light on the relationship between the two countries. What's going on, and where does the US stand?

events.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
events.description: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms has cast doubt on Anthropic's looming IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

events.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
events.description: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp says that midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

events.title: France among five major powers to represent EU in Ukraine talks
events.description: European Council President Antonio Costa on Friday said that Brussels will send diplomats from the bloc and five countries, including the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, to upcoming Ukraine talks.

events.title: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
events.description: China has been carrying out major military drills around Taiwan since early November. But contrary to some claims on social media, Beijing's armed forces have not actually implemented a blockade on the island; they just simulated it.

events.title: France asks Brussels to examine Algeria's non-compliance of EU association agreement
events.description: France announced on Friday that it will ask the European Commission to "examine" Algeria's non-compliance with its EU association agreement. Earlier in July, Algiers imposed a near-blanket ban on French imports, and last month, Algeria suspended urea shipments to France.

events.title: EU leaders choose team for Ukraine peace talks after months of wavering
events.description: British representatives will be part of a team representing Europe in Ukraine peace talks.

events.title: Man shot dead in Washington DC gym is named
events.description: A man shot dead in a Washington DC gym on Thursday has been named.

events.title: Wife of jailed ex-leader of Northern Ireland's largest pro-UK party put on sex offenders register
events.description: Eleanor Donaldson, the wife of former Northern Ireland unionist leader Jeffrey Donaldson, has been placed on the sex offenders register for five years

events.title: Nauru's president has no political opponents after all lawmakers joined the government side
events.description: Nauru’s president, David Adeang, has announced that all opposition lawmakers in parliament have joined his government

events.title: Passenger van plunges into river in northern Pakistan, killing 11 people
events.description: Officials say a passenger van veered off a mountainous road and plunged into a river in northern Pakistan, killing 11 people and injuring three others

events.title: Sheinbaum rebuts Trump, says no migrant caravans have reached US border since January 2025
events.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum says no migrant caravans have reached the U.S. border since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025

events.title: ‘Lives are at stake’: Humanitarians call for swift entry of winter supplies in Gaza
events.description: Winter supplies must enter the Gaza Strip where “lives are at stake”, the UN and partners said in an urgent appeal on Friday, in the wake of deadly rainfall this past weekend.

events.title: School investigating after viral video shows 10th grade girl punched, put in chokehold on Ohio school bus
events.description: Viral video shows a male student repeatedly punching, kicking and choking a 10th grade girl on an Ohio school bus as other students laughed.

events.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Cold case DNA unmasks 'Montauk Mary' as cops probe link to Jersey Shore 'Thrill Killer'
events.description: Sofia Margherita Marrone, known as "Montauk Mary" for decades, was identified via DNA and linked to Jersey Shore "Thrill Killer" Richard Biegenwald.

events.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: JonBenet Ramsey investigators are retesting evidence with newer technology, police chief says
events.description: Boulder investigators are retesting decades-old DNA evidence in the JonBenet Ramsey cold case using advanced technology that didn't exist in 1997.

events.title: DHS touts highest ICE deportations in history, as Mullin says agency has been ‘unleashed’
events.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced record ICE arrests and deportations in fiscal 2026, with arrests exceeding three Biden fiscal years combined.

events.title: Former owner of Peanut the squirrel, viral pet euthanized by NY officials, detained by ICE
events.description: Nearly two years after New York officials euthanized Peanut the squirrel, his former owners face another ordeal as Daniela Bittner remains in ICE custody.

events.title: Oklahoma man, 73, executed for plotting murder of lover's husband, offers no last words
events.description: James Pavatt was pronounced dead after lethal injection for plotting the 2001 murder of Rob Andrew, who was gunned down in his garage just before Thanksgiving.

events.title: WATCH: Deranged animal rights activist arrested after allegedly hitting carriage driver with skateboard
events.description: Video captures Abigail Holbrook allegedly striking a Central Park horse carriage driver with a skateboard while shouting about animal abuse.

events.title: Israel's political shake-up enters new phase as former PM plays kingmaker — and deadline looms
events.description: Benjamin Netanyahu called for unity, but Gadi Eisenkot canceled Likud talks after calling the outgoing prime minister's speech "delusional."

events.title: Israeli president taps Netanyahu rival to form government as coalition battle looms
events.description: Gadi Eisenkot secured 67 Knesset endorsements over Benjamin Netanyahu, but deep coalition divisions over Arab parties and conscription cloud his path.
